title: Affine PGL quotients with closed orbits and zero-dimensional stabilizers
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field], $r\geq1$, $G=\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ (invertible matrices modulo scalars), and $U=\operatorname{Spec}E$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] for a finitely generated commutative $k$-algebra $E$. Let $G$ act on $U$ by $k$-scheme morphisms, and write $E^G=\{e:\rho(e)=e\otimes1\}$ for the invariants of the induced coordinate coaction $\rho:E\to E\otimes_k k[G]$. Suppose that for every algebraically closed extension $\Omega/k$, every $G_\Omega$-orbit in $U_\Omega$ is closed and each stabilizer group scheme has dimension zero. Then the morphism $p:U\to\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)$ induced by $E^G\hookrightarrow E$ is invariant and surjective. For every algebraic space $T/k$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], composition with $p$ gives a bijection $\operatorname{Mor}_k(\operatorname{Spec}(E^G),T)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_k(U,T)^G$, where invariant means equality of the composites from $G\times_kU$ via the action and second projection. For every algebraically closed $\Omega/k$, $p$ gives $U(\Omega)/G(\Omega)\simeq\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)(\Omega)$. No reducedness, smoothness of stabilizers, or invertibility of their orders is assumed.

source.place: Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3, Theorems 9.1.4 and 9.7.6 (affine invariant adequate quotient), 5.3.1 (geometric fibres), 8.3.2 and Section 8.1 (quasi-finite separated diagonal implies finite inertia and the Keel--Mori coarse quotient), and 7.2.1 (comparison uniqueness). This is the affine finite-stabilizer consequence, not the unrestricted universality claim for general adequate moduli spaces. Local PDF WANTED; read online.

proof.text: Put $Y=\operatorname{Spec}(E^G)$ and $\mathcal X=[U/G]$, with atlas $\pi:U\to\mathcal X$. The affine-action presentation applies to $\operatorname{PGL}_{r,k}$ over this arbitrary field, including $r=1$. It gives the canonical map $\phi:\mathcal X\to Y$ with $\phi\pi=p$, and makes $\mathcal X$ finite type with affine, hence separated, diagonal. Its finite-geometric-fibre clause applies to the dimension-zero stabilizer hypothesis and gives a quasi-finite separated diagonal. In particular this uses group-scheme stabilizers, without replacing them by their reduced groups.

source.place: Tags 04TK, 04WZ, 04X0; spaces-groupoids.tex Tags 04M9 and 044U; action-groupoid presentation.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-pgl-geometric-reductivity] to all surjective equivariant maps of finitely generated $k$-algebras: it supplies precisely the positive-power invariant lifting required by [lem-sfb-power-lifting-adequate-affine-quotient]. That criterion makes the canonical $\phi$ an adequate moduli space. Its finite-type formulation is important: the criterion includes passage from finite-type invariant power lifting to the sheafwise adequate condition; that passage is not being assumed from the word reductive. The same PGL input also shows that $E^G$ is finitely generated, though the next criterion requires only that $Y$ be affine.

source.place: Lemma 9.2.5 and Theorem 9.1.4 with Remark 9.1.5; PGL input Theorem 9.7.6.

proof.text: The stack from step 1 and adequate map from step 2 satisfy the finite-diagonal criterion: $\mathcal X$ is finite type over $k$, its diagonal is quasi-finite and separated, and the target $Y$ is affine. Therefore $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ is finite and the inertia $I_{\mathcal X}\to\mathcal X$ is finite. This is the necessary uniform finiteness assertion; dimension zero of each stabilizer alone was not used to assert finite inertia.

source.place: Theorem 8.3.2, proof of (3) implies (1), for separated Y.

proof.text: The finite-inertia coarse-space theorem now gives a surjective coarse morphism $q:\mathcal X\to Q$, itself adequate. Since the diagonal of $\mathcal X/k$ is finite by step 3, its separatedness clause gives a separated algebraic space $Q/k$. The theorem supplies both universal factorization through $q$ for every algebraic-space target and the bijections on geometric isomorphism classes. It does not require $\mathcal X$ to be Deligne--Mumford, so nonreduced stabilizers in positive characteristic are allowed.

Compare the two adequate maps explicitly. Since $Q$ is separated, restricted adequate universality for $\phi$ gives a unique $\alpha:Y\to Q$ with $\alpha\phi=q$. Since $Y$ is a scheme, the same universality for $q$ gives a unique $\beta:Q\to Y$ with $\beta q=\phi$. Thus $(\beta\alpha)\phi=\phi$ and $(\alpha\beta)q=q$. Injectivity in the same two universal bijections, with targets $Y$ and $Q$, respectively, gives $\beta\alpha=\mathrm{id}_Y$ and $\alpha\beta=\mathrm{id}_Q$. Hence $\alpha$ is an isomorphism identifying $\phi$ with the coarse morphism. The identities are equalities of maps to algebraic spaces, so the harmless 2-isomorphisms on the stack introduce no choices.

source.place: Theorem 7.2.1, applied only to the separated space Q and the scheme Y; elementary uniqueness comparison.

proof.text: For an arbitrary algebraic space $T/k$, the coarse universal property and the isomorphism of step 5 give $\operatorname{Mor}_k(Y,T)\simeq\operatorname{Mor}_k(\mathcal X,T)$. The action-groupoid presentation identifies the second set with $\operatorname{Mor}_k(U,T)^G$, and the composite is precomposition with $\phi\pi=p$. The same presentation gives $U(\Omega)/G(\Omega)\simeq\pi_0(\mathcal X(\Omega))$; the coarse bijection followed by $\alpha^{-1}$ gives the asserted bijection with $Y(\Omega)$, induced by $p$. Finally $\pi$ and $q$ are surjective, hence so is $p=\alpha^{-1}q\pi$. Invariance follows directly on rings: for every $e\in E^G$, the two pullbacks along action and projection both equal $e\otimes1$. This proves all clauses. The closed-orbit assumption is consistent with, but not needed in addition to, the finite-diagonal adequate argument.

source.place: Tag 044U; examples-stacks.tex Tag 04WM; Alper Section 8 coarse-space definition and Theorem 8.1.1.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N8-99bccff81 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: The item statement is unchanged from Q37's version and is true: the Mumford/Seshadri geometric quotient by a geometrically reductive group. The item is not dropped and not superseded (unsplit in live and side-live), and there is no repair note. Alper arXiv:1005.2398v3 was fetched read-only and its text extracted. All six steps check out. (1) The [U/G] presentation gives a quasi-finite, separated, affine diagonal from the dim-0 stabilizers, via the pullback (a,pr2). (2) PGL power lifting matches the new criterion exactly (Alper 9.2.5(3')⇒(2), 9.1.4/Remark 9.1.5). (3) Alper 8.3.2 (3)⇒finite diagonal, read in its proof via Lemma 8.3.1, applies with Y affine; finite type and absolute vs relative diagonal both check. (4) Keel–Mori (Stacks 0DUT/0DUY, Alper 8.1.1/8.2.1) gives an adequate coarse space Q, separated because Δ is finite. (5) α comes from 7.2.1 with Q separated, β from q's universality; both inverse identities follow by injectivity. (6) Transport to Mor(U,T)^G and to geometric points uses triviality of smooth torsors over algebraically closed fields; p=α⁻¹qπ is surjective. Edge cases checked: r=1, left translation, μ_p stabilizers. All seven new nodes are true and none restates the item. The duplicate search found nothing: the existing DM coarse-moduli nodes assume a coarse scheme is already given. FIX: def-sfb-adequate-moduli-space only required power lifting for algebras on 𝒳 with sections over étale W→Y. That is not Alper's adequately-affine notion (Def 4.1.1) for non-affine Y, which lem-sfb-adequate-locally-separated-universality (7.2.1) needs. I rewrote it to require lifting for all quasi-coherent algebras on each 𝒳_W, equivalent by Alper 4.2.1(3),(4), Remark 4.1.3 and Lemma 4.1.8(3)⇔(2), and updated source.place to match; stmt_deps are unchanged.
